newsitem.title: USA: $25 million settles Alaska pipeline tariff case.
newsitem.headline: $25 million settles Alaska pipeline tariff case.

text.p: The state of Alaska will get $25 million from owners of the Trans Alaska Pipeline System in a settlement that resolves a dispute over pipeline tariffs, Alaska Attorney General Bruce Botelho said Friday.
The settlement also creates a system for resolving future disputes over tariffs, the charge assessed for transporting oil through the 800-mile pipeline, Botelho said.
The dispute resolved by the agreement concerns the state's challenge to tariffs charged from 1994 to 1997 to cover costs of repairing and upgrading the pipeline's electrical systems.
The settlement includes provisions for arbitration over future disputes, Botelho said.
Under Alaska's tax and royalty system, the state effectively pays a quarter of the tariffs -- including the cost of running the oil pipeline -- through reduced revenues, state officials said.
Major owners of the trans-Alaska pipeline are British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield and Exxon. Phillips Petroleum, Unocal, Mobil and Amerada Hess own minor shares.
